name: Delft University of Technology
about: The Netherlands' oldest and largest technical university, on a campus of its own south of the medieval centre of Delft, twenty minutes from The Hague and an hour from Amsterdam. Seventeen three-year BSc programmes, of which four are taught fully in English: Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering, Earth, Climate and Technology, and Nanobiology. Three of those four are numerus fixus, which means an IB student's realistic Delft shortlist is decided on 15 January rather than in July.

languageOfInstruction.note: TU Delft states: "only four programmes are offered fully in English; Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering, Earth, Climate and Technology and Nanobiology." The other thirteen BSc programmes are taught in Dutch, and Computer Science and Engineering also runs a bilingual Dutch-English track that a foreign diploma does not open.

notes: TU Delft publishes its IB entry requirements in IB terms and in a single table covering every BSc programme, which is the cleanest example found in the Netherlands of the pattern ADR 0002 predicts: no local scale, no conversion, nothing to translate.

The university accepts only Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at HL. Applications and Interpretation is not accepted at any level for any programme, and the page says so once, at the top of the IB table, rather than on each row.
TU Delft also states it does not accept students with an IB Career-related Programme certificate.

The Aerospace Engineering selection pages carried last year's procedure when read on 2026-09-23 and say the 2027-2028 setup will appear before 19 December 2026. The Computer Science and Engineering pages were already updated for 2027-2028.
